approach: No author implementation is available, so the plan reimplements only the match-target claim C1 with public QM7b data and scikit-learn. It downloads the QM7b .mat file, loads the 7,211 x 14 property matrix and the atomic-charge matrix, derives total atom count including hydrogens, z-scores the properties on the full dataset, performs a fixed-seed 90/10 split, fits a single CART regression tree constrained to 101 leaves, and evaluates test MSE/RMSE/MAE/Pearson R. A smoke mode and sanity baselines are included; QM9, tree-SNE, SUOD, and intrinsic-dimension claims are intentionally out of scope for this budget.

files.purpose: Pin the small CPU dependency set: numpy, scipy, pandas, scikit-learn, requests.
Package marker for importable source modules.
Single source of truth for dataset URLs, expected shapes, split seed, model hyperparameters, tolerance, and output paths.
Download qm7b.mat using requests with mirror fallbacks, validate file size, and record SHA-256.
Load qm7b.mat with scipy.io.loadmat, extract X and Z, derive atom counts, z-score X, perform the 90/10 split, and return numpy arrays plus metadata.
Build and fit the DecisionTreeRegressor constrained to 101 leaves, expose n_leaves and feature importances.
Compute MSE, RMSE, MAE, Pearson R, tolerance checks, and write the final metrics JSON.
CLI entrypoint: full run writes results/metrics.json; --smoke runs a tiny data-flow check and writes results/smoke_metrics.json.

preprocessing.feature_scaling: StandardScaler fit on full X before split; zero mean, unit variance (R2/R3; A3)
preprocessing.target: number of atoms including hydrogens, derived from Z > 0 per row; raw counts, not z-scored (R4; A4/A7)

metrics.R_definition: Pearson correlation coefficient between y_true and y_pred (A6)
metrics.nbrOfRules_definition: number of terminal leaves in the fitted tree (A12)

steps: Create the project skeleton and requirements.txt; confirm numpy, scipy, pandas, scikit-learn, and requests are importable.
Implement src/config.py with the QM7b URLs, expected shapes, preprocessing choices, seed 0, DecisionTreeRegressor(max_leaf_nodes=101), and output paths.
Implement src/download.py: try each configured URL with requests, stream to data/qm7b.mat, verify file size is plausible (>1 MB), and compute SHA-256.

Implement src/data.py: load data/qm7b.mat with scipy.io.loadmat; inspect keys; extract X, transpose if shape is (14,7211), and validate it becomes (7211,14); extract Z and derive y=(Z>0).sum(axis=1), with a clear error if Z is absent; validate y is integer, finite, and max <= 23.

In src/data.py, fit StandardScaler on the full X matrix, transform X, then call train_test_split with test_size=0.1, random_state=0, shuffle=True; return X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test, scaler, and metadata.
Implement src/model.py: instantiate DecisionTreeRegressor(criterion='squared_error', max_leaf_nodes=101, random_state=0), fit on training data, and expose tree_.n_leaves and feature_importances_.

Implement src/evaluate.py: compute MSE, RMSE, MAE, Pearson R via np.corrcoef, and nbrOfRules; compare MSE to the 10% band; assemble a JSON object containing observed metrics, paper values, split sizes, model config, assumptions A1/A2/A3/A4/A6/A7/A12/A13, and download SHA-256.

Implement reproduce.py with --smoke: full mode loads/downloads QM7b, fits the 101-leaf tree, evaluates on the test split, and writes results/metrics.json; smoke mode uses the first 200 rows, an 80/20 split, and max_leaf_nodes=20, then writes results/smoke_metrics.json.
Run the smoke test first and verify shapes, finite values, integer targets, and that the smoke tree has <=20 leaves.

Run the full command python reproduce.py and verify nbrOfRules is exactly 101 and test MSE is inside [0.12573, 0.15367]. If MSE is outside but nbrOfRules is correct, record the primary result and optionally run a documented seed-sweep diagnostic (seeds 0-4) without changing the official seed-0 metric.
Inspect results/metrics.json for all required C1 fields and confirm the file is valid JSON.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: downloads/loads QM7b if needed, takes the first 200 rows, z-scores 14 features, does an 80/20 split, fits DecisionTreeRegressor(max_leaf_nodes=20), prints X shapes, target min/max, finite checks, n_leaves, and writes results/smoke_metrics.json.
intermediate_checks: Downloaded data/qm7b.mat exists, size is plausible, and SHA-256 is recorded.
scipy.io.loadmat exposes X with shape (7211,14) after any needed transpose; no NaN or inf values; all 14 columns are nonconstant.
Z has first dimension 7211; derived atom counts are positive integers, max <= 23, and include hydrogens (some atomic numbers equal 1).
Report atom-count min/max/mean/std and confirm the distribution is consistent with QM7b molecules of up to 23 atoms including hydrogens.
After StandardScaler, feature means are approximately 0 and standard deviations approximately 1.
Train/test split sizes are 6489/722 and train/test target means and standard deviations are similar.
The full tree has n_leaves == 101; record depth and top feature importances.
Sanity baselines: mean-predictor test MSE equals test-target variance; a LinearRegression baseline is fit for comparison; the tree MSE should be far below the mean baseline and near 0.1397.
All reported metrics are finite, Pearson R is in [-1,1], and the 10% tolerance check is explicitly stored in the JSON.
budget_plan: About 10 minutes total on CPU: 2-3 minutes for environment checks and QM7b download, <1 minute for the smoke run, <1 minute for the full 101-leaf tree fit/evaluation, and 2-3 minutes for sanity baselines/inspection/JSON validation. No GPU is needed. If the primary seed-0 MSE is outside tolerance, a 2-minute optional seed-sweep diagnostic is allowed, but the official output remains the fixed-seed C1 run.
